subject: Follow-up: performance handoff & load-run next steps for OperaSoft
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Choi <achoi@operasoft.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: performance handoff & load-run next steps for OperaSoft

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led load run scheduled and guarded by the SLOs we discussed.

Recap (high level)
- Goal: validate streaming and non-streaming SLOs for OperaSoft chat routing features (p95 latency targets, concurrent streaming sessions).
- Test harness: customer will run k6 (xk6-websockets) against Redwood staging endpoints we provide; Redwood will create a short-lived test account and provide allowlist IPs.
- Targets you mentioned: 800–1,000 concurrent streaming sessions peak; p95 framing latency target of ~700ms for streaming; non-streaming p95 <= 250ms at expected qps.

Next steps (action items & owners)
1) Redwood (Monica) — provide staging endpoints, test credentials, a reference k6 script and notes for websockets + recommended ramp schedule. Attachment: opera-k6-probe-v1.js (initial probe).
2) OperaSoft (Alex) — confirm load generator source IPs for allowlist and preferred test window(s). Please also copy your firewall/contact (you mentioned secops@operasoft.com).
3) Redwood (Rafael) — share a proposed 4-hour window and rollback plan; monitor metrics and be on the call for the first hour.
4) Both — document success criteria (p95, error rate threshold, throughput floor) before the run.

Suggested test windows (ET):
- Tue Aug 25, 10:00–14:00 ET (preferred)
- Wed Aug 26, 10:00–14:00 ET (backup)

Quick questions for you:
- Do you need us to expose a non-streaming endpoint for tokenized bulk requests during the same window (we can host both)?
- Who will be your load-run owner (name & mobile) so we can be on the same call?

If this looks right I’ll have Monica drop the staging details and the xk6 notes.

Thanks,
Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
(attachment: opera-k6-probe-v1.js)
From: Alex Choi <achoi@operasoft.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@operasoft.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance handoff & load-run next steps for OperaSoft

Rafael — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few things from our side and answering your questions:

- We do want both streaming (websocket framing) and non-streaming (HTTP text generation) endpoints available during the run.
- OperaSoft expected acceptance criteria: streaming sustained 800 concurrent sessions for 60 minutes, p95 framing latency <= 700ms, error rate < 0.5%. For non-streaming, target p95 <= 250ms at 120 requests/sec.
- Load-run owner: Alex Choi (me) — mobile +1 (555) 213-9876; firewall contact: secops@operasoft.com (please loop them into allowlist communication).

Allowlist — our load generators will come from these IP ranges (please whitelist):
- 52.23.144.0/24
- 35.175.200.14

Preferred window: Wed Aug 26, 10:00–14:00 ET (we can shift to Aug 25 if needed but prefer the 26th).

Two asks:
1) We need bearer tokens that live for at least 3 hours (or a client-provided API key) so our k6 processes can run without interruption.
2) Any recommended k6/session ramp schedule you suggest for hitting 800 concurrent streams while preserving the p95 target?

I’ll get secops on a thread if you need firewall-level proofs.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the staging details.

—Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
OperaSoft
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Choi <achoi@operasoft.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance handoff & load-run next steps for OperaSoft

Alex — thanks, this is perfect. Below are the staging details and technical guidance for the k6/xk6 websoc ket probe. I’ve included the reference patch to enable keep-alive frames for the xk6 websocket helper.

Staging endpoints and auth
- Streaming (websocket): wss://staging-infer.redwood.ai/opera-stream/v1
- Non-streaming (HTTP): https://staging-infer.redwood.ai/opera-chat/v1/generate
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer <TEST_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER>
- Test account: opera-staging-client (we’ll issue tokens with 'scope:stream' and 'scope:nonstream'). Token lifetime: 4 hours (we can shorten if needed).

Allowlist request (what we need from you)
- Please confirm the exact egress IPs for your k6 runners. We received the ranges earlier — OK to add 52.23.144.0/24 and 35.175.200.14. We will also provide a short list of Redwood egress IPs if you need inbound firewall rules on your side.

Recommended k6 approach (practical notes)
- Use xk6-websockets for the streaming probe (https://github.com/xk6-plugins/xk6-websocket). The attached opera-k6-probe-v1.js demonstrates opening N sockets and sending short keepalive/turn messages consistent with your production framing.
- Ramp: start with 200 concurrent sockets for 10 minutes, then increase by 150 every 10 minutes until you reach 800. Hold 800 for 60 minutes, then ramp down over 20 minutes. This helps isolate pacing vs. platform saturation.
- Non-streaming: target 120 rps with a steady Poisson arrival; run a 15-minute steady-state window after a 10-minute warm-up.
- Token handling: use a single bearer token per k6 worker process. We’ll provide a token per runner if you prefer IP-bound tokens.
- Metrics we’ll monitor in real time: p95 latency (stream framing & initial response), overall error rate, headroom (% CPU/GPU utilization), and per-request token cost. We’ll publish a live dashboard link when the run starts.

Attachments / helpers
- Attached: k6-websocket-helper.patch (small patch to the helper that adjusts default ping interval) and opera-k6-probe-v1.js.
- Drive folder with scripts: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-opera-k6

Operational notes / rollback
- We will keep a canary pool active and auto-fallback to a lower-capacity model if error rate exceeds 1% for more than 5 minutes. If that triggers, we’ll pause the run and engage your team.
- We will also post a short-run summary in the drive folder within 30 minutes of the window closing.

Let me know if you want us to issue tokens now for a connectivity smoke test prior to the full window.

—Monica
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
(attachment: k6-websocket-helper.patch)
From: Alex Choi <achoi@operasoft.com>

I’ll drop a calendar invite for Aug 26 09:45 ET to do a 15-minute connectivity smoke test and then the full window starting at 10:00 ET. Secops copied.

See you on the smoke test.

—Alex
